- `VAR_NAME` → the variable/identifier name; `VAR_NUMBER` → line number or numeric value; `VAR_RESERVED_WORD` → keyword; `VAR_OPERATOR` → operator; `VAR_FILE` → filename.

3: //! ```mlt
4: //! id = "BUGS_ENGINE"
5: //! title = "Bugs"
6: //! category = "bugs"

13: //! ## Rule
14: //!
15: //! Detects likely bugs and logic errors in MATLAB code. All 35 checks share a
16: //! single hybrid engine (`BugsEngine`) that performs both node-level checking
17: //! (dispatched per-node during traversal) and file-level checking (full-tree
18: //! analysis after traversal). Each diagnostic carries the specific check ID
19: //! (e.g. `IFBDUP`, `FNAN`).
20: //!
21: //! ## Check IDs
22: //!
23: //! | Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description |
24: //! | --- | --- | --- | --- |

61: //! ## Fix
62: //!
63: //! Rewrites the flagged construct into the safe equivalent. For example:
64: //!
65: //! - `&` → `&&` and `|` → `||` in boolean contexts.
66: //! - `x == NaN` → `isnan(x)` (and `x ~= NaN` → `~isnan(x)`).
67: //! - `length(x) == 0` → `isempty(x)` and `size(x) == [m n]` → `isequal(size(x), [m n])`.
68: //! - Bare function names on the RHS of an assignment get an `@` prefix.
69: //! - Duplicate boolean conditions are collapsed (`a && a` → `a`).

79: //! while true
80: //!     % infinite

82: //! ```
83: //!
84: //! ### Correct

86: //! ```matlab
87: //! if isnan(x)
88: //!     disp('not a number');
89: //! end
90: //! while true % intentional
91: //!     % ...
92: //! end
93: //! ```

242:     fn walk_if_branch_dup_bodies(node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
243:         if node.kind() == "if_statement" {
244:             let mut branch_bodies: Vec<(String, Node)> = Vec::new();
245: 
246:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
247:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
248:                 let body = match child.kind() {
249:                     "block" => Some(child),
250:                     "elseif_clause" | "else_clause" => find_block_child(child),
251:                     _ => None,
252:                 };
253: 
254:                 if let Some(body_node) = body {
255:                     let body_text = normalize_whitespace(node_text(body_node, source));
256:                     if let Some((_, first_node)) =
257:                         branch_bodies.iter().find(|(t, _)| *t == body_text)
258:                     {
259:                         let pos = child.start_position();
260:                         let _ = first_node;
261:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
262:                             rule_id: "IFBDUP",
263:                             message: "Duplicate if-branch body; branches have identical code"
264:                                 .to_string(),
265:                             severity: Severity::Error,
266:                             byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.end_byte(),
267:                             line: pos.row + 1,
268:                             column: pos.column + 1,
269:                             fix: None,
270:                         });
271:                     } else {
272:                         branch_bodies.push((body_text, child));
273:                     }
274:                 }
275:             }
276:         }
277: 
278:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
279:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
280:             Self::walk_if_branch_dup_bodies(child, source, diagnostics);
281:         }
282:     }

295:             // Collect the main if condition.

588:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,

590:         if node.kind() == "identifier" {
591:             let name = node_text(node, source).trim();
592:             if name == "varargin" && !has_varargin {
593:                 let pos = node.start_position();
594:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
595:                     rule_id: "VARARG",
596:                     message: "'varargin' used in function that does not declare it as input"
597:                         .to_string(),
598:                     severity: Severity::Error,
599:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
600:                     line: pos.row + 1,
601:                     column: pos.column + 1,
602:                     fix: None,
603:                 });
604:             } else if name == "varargout" && !has_varargout {
605:                 let pos = node.start_position();
606:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
607:                     rule_id: "VARARG",
608:                     message: "'varargout' used in function that does not declare it as output"
609:                         .to_string(),
610:                     severity: Severity::Error,
611:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
612:                     line: pos.row + 1,
613:                     column: pos.column + 1,
614:                     fix: None,
615:                 });
616:             }
617:         }
618: 
619:         // Don't recurse into nested function definitions.
620:         if node.kind() == "function_definition" {
621:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
622:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
623:                 if child.kind() != "function_definition" {
624:                     Self::check_vararg_in_body(
625:                         child,
626:                         source,
627:                         has_varargin,
628:                         has_varargout,
629:                         diagnostics,
630:                     );
631:                 }
632:             }
633:         } else {
634:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
635:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
636:                 Self::check_vararg_in_body(child, source, has_varargin, has_varargout, diagnostics);
637:             }
638:         }
639:     }

641:     /// Parfor-related checks: PFUIXE, PFBFN, PFWHOS, PFTUSE, PFRNC.
642:     fn check_parfor_issues(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
643:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
644:         Self::walk_parfor_issues(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
645:         diagnostics

648:     fn walk_parfor_issues(node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
649:         if node.kind() == "for_statement" {
650:             let stmt_text = node_text(node, source);
651:             if !stmt_text.starts_with("parfor") {
652:                 // Not a parfor — check if it could be one (FWPARF).
653:                 if could_be_parfor(node, source) {
654:                     let pos = node.start_position();
655:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
656:                         rule_id: "FWPARF",
657:                         message:
658:                             "For loop could potentially be converted to parfor for parallelism"
659:                                 .to_string(),
660:                         severity: Severity::Error,
661:                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
662:                         line: pos.row + 1,
663:                         column: pos.column + 1,
664:                         fix: None,
665:                     });
666:                 }
667: 
668:                 // Recurse into children.
669:                 let mut cursor = node.walk();
670:                 for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
671:                     Self::walk_parfor_issues(child, source, diagnostics);
672:                 }
673:                 return;
674:             }
675: 
676:             // This is a parfor. Extract the loop variable.
677:             let loop_var = extract_for_variable(node, source);
678: 
679:             // Walk the parfor body for issues.
680:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
681:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
682:                 if child.kind() == "block" {
683:                     Self::check_parfor_body(child, source, loop_var.as_deref(), diagnostics);
684:                 }
685:             }
686: 
687:             // PFTRIV: Check if parfor could just be a for loop (body is trivial).
688:             if is_trivial_parfor(node, source) {
689:                 let pos = node.start_position();
690:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
691:                     rule_id: "PFTRIV",
692:                     message: "Parfor loop body is trivial; consider using regular for loop"
693:                         .to_string(),
694:                     severity: Severity::Error,
695:                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
696:                     line: pos.row + 1,
697:                     column: pos.column + 1,
698:                     fix: None,
699:                 });
700:             }
701:         }
702: 
703:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
704:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
705:             Self::walk_parfor_issues(child, source, diagnostics);
706:         }
707:     }

709:     fn check_parfor_body(
710:         node: Node,
711:         source: &str,
712:         loop_var: Option<&str>,
713:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
714:     ) {
715:         match node.kind() {
716:             "function_call" => {
717:                 let func_name = extract_call_name(node, source);
718:                 if let Some(name) = &func_name {
719:                     // PFUIXE: Loop variable used in eval.
720:                     if *name == "eval" || *name == "evalin" || *name == "feval" {
721:                         if let Some(lv) = loop_var {
722:                             let args = collect_call_args(node, source);
723:                             if args.iter().any(|a| a.contains(lv)) {
724:                                 let pos = node.start_position();
725:                                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
726:                                     rule_id: "PFUIXE",
727:                                     message: format!(
728:                                         "Parfor index variable '{lv}' used in {name}; \
729:                                          this is not allowed in parfor"
730:                                     ),
731:                                     severity: Severity::Error,
732:                                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
733:                                     line: pos.row + 1,
734:                                     column: pos.column + 1,
735:                                     fix: None,
736:                                 });
737:                             }
738:                         }
739:                     }
740: 
741:                     // PFWHOS: who/whos in parfor.
742:                     if *name == "who" || *name == "whos" {
743:                         let pos = node.start_position();
744:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
745:                             rule_id: "PFWHOS",
746:                             message: format!("'{name}' is not allowed inside parfor loops"),
747:                             severity: Severity::Error,
748:                             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
749:                             line: pos.row + 1,
750:                             column: pos.column + 1,
751:                             fix: None,
752:                         });
753:                     }
754: 
755:                     // PFBFN: Certain builtin functions problematic in parfor.
756:                     let problematic_builtins = [
757:                         "assignin",
758:                         "evalin",
759:                         "save",
760:                         "load",
761:                         "clear",
762:                         "global",
763:                         "persistent",
764:                     ];
765:                     if problematic_builtins.contains(name) {
766:                         let pos = node.start_position();
767:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
768:                             rule_id: "PFBFN",
769:                             message: format!(
770:                                 "Function '{name}' may not behave as expected inside parfor"
771:                             ),
772:                             severity: Severity::Error,
773:                             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
774:                             line: pos.row + 1,
775:                             column: pos.column + 1,
776:                             fix: None,
777:                         });
778:                     }
779:                 }
780:             }
781:             "assignment" => {
782:                 // PFTUSE / PFRNC: Check for temporary variable misuse and
783:                 // inconsistent reduction patterns.
784:                 if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left").or_else(|| node.child(0)) {
785:                     if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
786:                         let var_name = node_text(lhs, source).trim().to_string();
787:                         if let Some(rhs) =
788:                             node.child_by_field_name("right").or_else(|| node.child(2))
789:                         {
790:                             let rhs_text = node_text(rhs, source);
791:                             // PFTUSE: Variable used on both sides but is not a reduction.
792:                             if rhs_text.contains(&var_name)
793:                                 && !is_reduction_pattern(&var_name, rhs, source)
794:                             {
795:                                 let pos = node.start_position();
796:                                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
797:                                     rule_id: "PFTUSE",
798:                                     message: format!(
799:                                         "Temporary variable '{var_name}' used on both sides of \
800:                                          assignment in parfor; ensure correct classification"
801:                                     ),
802:                                     severity: Severity::Error,
803:                                     byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
804:                                     line: pos.row + 1,
805:                                     column: pos.column + 1,
806:                                     fix: None,
807:                                 });
808:                             }
809: 
810:                             // PFRNC: Reduction operator not consistent.
811:                             if is_reduction_pattern(&var_name, rhs, source) {
812:                                 // Check for mixed reduction operators on same variable.
813:                                 // This is a simplified check — full analysis would track
814:                                 // across the entire parfor body.
815:                                 if has_mixed_reduction_ops(&var_name, rhs, source) {
816:                                     let pos = node.start_position();
817:                                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
818:                                         rule_id: "PFRNC",
819:                                         message: format!(
820:                                             "Reduction variable '{var_name}' uses inconsistent \
821:                                              operators in parfor"
822:                                         ),
823:                                         severity: Severity::Error,
824:                                         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
825:                                         line: pos.row + 1,
826:                                         column: pos.column + 1,
827:                                         fix: None,
828:                                     });
829:                                 }
830:                             }
831:                         }
832:                     }
833:                 }
834:             }
835:             _ => {}
836:         }
837: 
838:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
839:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
840:             Self::check_parfor_body(child, source, loop_var, diagnostics);
841:         }
842:     }
843: }

951: /// Find the condition child of an `if_statement` or `elseif_clause` node.
952: ///
953: /// In tree-sitter-matlab, the condition is typically the node between the
954: /// keyword (`if`/`elseif`/`while`) and the body.
955: pub(crate) fn find_condition_child(node: Node) -> Option<Node> {
956:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
957:     let mut found_keyword = false;
958:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
959:         if child.kind() == "if"
960:             || child.kind() == "elseif"
961:             || child.kind() == "while"
962:             || child.is_named() && found_keyword
963:         {
964:             if found_keyword && child.kind() != "block" && child.kind() != "end" {
965:                 return Some(child);
966:             }
967:             if !child.is_named() || child.kind() == "if" || child.kind() == "while" {
968:                 found_keyword = true;
969:             }
970:         }
971:     }
972: 
973:     // Fallback: return the first named child that is not a keyword or block.
974:     let mut cursor2 = node.walk();
975:     let result = node.children(&mut cursor2).find(|child| {
976:         child.is_named()
977:             && child.kind() != "block"
978:             && child.kind() != "elseif_clause"
979:             && child.kind() != "else_clause"
980:             && child.kind() != "end"
981:             && child.kind() != "comment"
982:     });
983:     result
984: }

988:     let mut cursor = node.walk();

991:         .find(|child| child.kind() == "block");

1016: /// Extract the function name from a `function_call` node.
1017: pub(crate) fn extract_call_name<'a>(node: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
1018:     if node.kind() != "function_call" {
1019:         return None;
1020:     }
1021: 
1022:     // Try the `name` field first.
1023:     if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
1024:         if name_node.kind() == "identifier" {
1025:             return Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()]);
1026:         }
1027:         // For field_expression (e.g., obj.method), return the full text.
1028:         return Some(&source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()]);
1029:     }
1030: 
1031:     // Fallback: first identifier child.
1032:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
1033:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1034:         if child.kind() == "identifier" {
1035:             return Some(&source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()]);
1036:         }
1037:     }
1038: 
1039:     None
1040: }

1042: /// Collect arguments from a `function_call` node as text strings.
1043: pub(crate) fn collect_call_args<'a>(node: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Vec<&'a str> {

1050:                 if arg.is_named() {
1051:                     args.push(&source[arg.start_byte()..arg.end_byte()]);
1052:                 }
1053:             }
1054:             return args;
1055:         }
1056:     }
1057:     args

1066: /// Find the operator text in a binary/boolean/comparison operator node.
1067: pub(crate) fn find_operator_text<'a>(node: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> String {
1068:     // The operator is typically the second child (index 1), which is an
1069:     // anonymous node containing the operator symbol.
1070:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
1071:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
1072:         if !child.is_named() {
1073:             let text = &source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()];
1074:             let trimmed = text.trim();
1075:             if !trimmed.is_empty() && trimmed != "(" && trimmed != ")" && trimmed != "," {
1076:                 return trimmed.to_string();
1077:             }
1078:         }
1079:     }
1080: 
1081:     // Fallback: try the operator field.
1082:     if let Some(op_node) = node.child_by_field_name("operator") {
1083:         return node_text(op_node, source).trim().to_string();
1084:     }
1085: 
1086:     // Last resort: parse from the full text.
1087:     let text = node_text(node, source);
1088:     for op in &[
1089:         "&&", "||", "==", "~=", ">=", "<=", ">", "<", ".+", ".-", ".*", "./", ".\\", ".^", "+",
1090:         "-", "*", "/", "\\", "^", "&", "|",
1091:     ] {
1092:         if text.contains(op) {
1093:             return (*op).to_string();
1094:         }
1095:     }
1096: 
1097:     String::new()
1098: }

1102:     let mut current = node.parent();
1103:     while let Some(parent) = current {
1104:         if parent.kind() == "for_statement" || parent.kind() == "while_statement" {
1105:             return true;
1106:         }
1107:         current = parent.parent();

1112: /// Check if a node is in a boolean context (condition of if/while/elseif).
1113: pub(crate) fn is_in_boolean_context(node: Node) -> bool {
1114:     let mut current = node.parent();
1115:     while let Some(parent) = current {
1116:         match parent.kind() {
1117:             "if_statement" | "while_statement" | "elseif_clause" => {
1118:                 // Check if the node is in the condition part, not the body.
1119:                 // The condition comes before the first block child.
1120:                 let in_condition = true;
1121:                 let mut cursor = parent.walk();
1122:                 for child in parent.children(&mut cursor) {
1123:                     if child.kind() == "block" {
1124:                         break;
1125:                     }
1126:                     if child.id() == node.id() || is_ancestor_of(child, node) {
1127:                         return in_condition;
1128:                     }
1129:                 }
1130:                 return false;
1131:             }
1132:             // Stop at statement boundaries.
1133:             "source_file" | "function_definition" => return false,
1134:             _ => {}
1135:         }
1136:         current = parent.parent();
1137:     }
1138:     false
1139: }

1: //! # FORMATTING_ENGINE: Formatting Suggestion Checks
2: //!
3: //! ```mlt
4: //! id = "FORMATTING_ENGINE"
5: //! title = "Formatting Suggestion Checks"
6: //! category = "formatting"
7: //! severity = "info"
8: //! fix = true
9: //! icon = "lucide/align-left"
10: //! slug = "formatting"
11: //! ```
12: //!
13: //! ## Rule
14: //!
15: //! Suggests formatting improvements for MATLAB code. All 7 checks share a
16: //! single `FormattingEngine` that runs as a file-level rule, walking the whole
17: //! tree once and applying every enabled check per node. Each diagnostic
18: //! carries the specific check ID (e.g. `NOCOMMA`, `NO4LP`). Individual checks
19: //! can be enabled, disabled, or reconfigured through their own
20: //! `[lint.rules.*]` tables.
21: //!
22: //! ## Check IDs
23: //!
24: //! | Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description |
25: //! | --- | --- | --- | --- |
26: //! | NOCOMMA | info | yes | Extra comma is unnecessary. |
27: //! | NO4LP | info | yes | Parentheses are not needed in a FOR statement. |
28: //! | ALIGN | info | yes | This keyword might not be aligned with its matching END on line VAR_NUMBER. |
29: //! | NOPTS | info | yes | Add a semicolon after the statement to hide the output (in a script). |
30: //! | NOPRT | info | yes | Add a semicolon after the statement to hide the output (in a function). |
31: //! | PRTCAL | info | yes | Add a semicolon after the function call to hide the output. |
32: //! | NCOMMA | info | yes | Best practice is to separate output variables with commas. |
33: //!
34: //! ## Fix
35: //!
36: //! Each check rewrites the flagged construct directly:
37: //!
38: //! - NOCOMMA inserts a comma between space-separated row elements (`[1 2 3]` → `[1, 2, 3]`).
39: //! - NCOMMA inserts a comma between space-separated function arguments.
40: //! - NO4LP rewrites the indentation prefix of misindented statements.
41: //! - ALIGN re-indents `elseif`/`else` clauses to the column of their `if`.
42: //! - NOPTS and NOPRT strip unnecessary parentheses (`(x)` → `x`).
43: //! - PRTCAL rewrites a string-only call to command syntax (`disp('hello')` → `disp hello`).
44: //!
45: //! ## Examples
46: //!
47: //! ### Incorrect
48: //!
49: //! ```matlab
50: //! x = [1 2 3];
51: //! y = (a);
52: //! if (x > 0)
53: //!     disp('hello');
54: //! end
55: //! ```
56: //!
57: //! ### Correct
58: //!
59: //! ```matlab
60: //! x = [1, 2, 3];
61: //! y = a;
62: //! if x > 0
63: //!     disp hello;
64: //! end
65: //! ```
66: //!
67: //! ### Fixed
68: //!
69: //! ```diff
70: //! - x = [1 2 3];
71: //! + x = [1, 2, 3];
72: //! - y = (a);
73: //! + y = a;
74: //! - if (x > 0)
75: //! + if x > 0
76: //! ```
77: //!
78: //! ## Configuration
79: //!
80: //! Each check is configured independently through its own rule table:
81: //!
82: //! ```toml
83: //! [lint.rules.NOCOMMA]
84: //! severity = "info"
85: //!
86: //! [lint.rules.NO4LP]
87: //! severity = "info"
88: //! indent_size = 4

244: impl FormattingEngine {
245:     /// Walk the tree recursively, applying enabled checks to each node.
246:     fn visit_recursive(&self, node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
247:         let kind = node.kind();
248:         // Note: multiple checks can apply to the same node type, so dispatch
249:         // each independently rather than using mutually-exclusive match arms.

251:         // NOCOMMA: matrix/cell rows with space-separated elements
252:         if (kind == "matrix" || kind == "cell") && self.enabled.nocomma {
253:             self.check_nocomma(node, source, diagnostics);
254:         }
255: 
256:         // NO4LP: indentation in loop/conditional bodies
257:         if matches!(
258:             kind,
259:             "for_statement" | "while_statement" | "if_statement" | "switch_statement"
260:         ) && self.enabled.no4lp
261:         {
262:             self.check_no4lp(node, source, diagnostics);
263:         }
264: 
265:         // ALIGN: elseif/else alignment with parent if
266:         if kind == "if_statement" && self.enabled.align {
267:             self.check_align(node, source, diagnostics);
268:         }
269: 
270:         // NOPTS: unnecessary parentheses around condition
271:         if matches!(kind, "if_statement" | "while_statement") && self.enabled.nopts {
272:             self.check_nopts(node, source, diagnostics);
273:         }
274: 
275:         // NOPRT: unnecessary parentheses around simple expressions
276:         if kind == "parenthesis" && self.enabled.noprt {
277:             self.check_noprt(node, source, diagnostics);
278:         }
279: 
280:         // PRTCAL: function syntax that could be command syntax
281:         if kind == "function_call" && self.enabled.prtcal {

283:         }

286:         if kind == "function_call" && self.enabled.ncomma {

288:         }

290:         // Recurse into children.
291:         let child_count = node.child_count();
292:         for i in 0..child_count {
293:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
294:                 self.visit_recursive(child, source, diagnostics);
295:             }
296:         }
297:     }

345:     let child_count = paren_node.child_count();

350:             .strip_prefix('(')
351:             .and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix(')'))
352:             .unwrap_or(text)
353:             .to_string();

355:     // Content is between the opening "(" and closing ")" nodes.
356:     let start = paren_node.start_byte() + 1; // skip "("
357:     let end = paren_node.end_byte().saturating_sub(1); // skip ")"
358:     source[start..end].trim().to_string()

376:         if inner.is_some() {

378:         }
379:         inner = Some(child);

1: //! NCOMMA check: use comma to separate input arguments.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
6: // NCOMMA: Use comma to separate input arguments
7: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
8: 
9: impl FormattingEngine {
10:     /// For `function_call` arguments, check if args are separated by spaces
11:     /// instead of commas.
12:     pub(crate) fn check_ncomma(&self, node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
13:         let Some(args_node) = find_arguments_child(node) else {
14:             return;
15:         };
16: 
17:         // Walk argument children looking for adjacent expressions without commas.
18:         let mut prev_expr: Option<Node> = None;
19:         let arg_count = args_node.child_count();
20: 
21:         for i in 0..arg_count {
22:             let Some(child) = args_node.child(i) else {
23:                 continue;
24:             };
25:             let kind = child.kind();
26: 
27:             // Reset on comma. A zero-width comma token is inserted by the
28:             // grammar when an argument separator is missing.
29:             if kind == "," {
30:                 if child.start_byte() == child.end_byte() {
31:                     let pos = child.start_position();
32:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
33:                         rule_id: "NCOMMA",
34:                         message: "Use comma to separate input arguments".to_string(),
35:                         severity: Severity::Info,
36:                         byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.start_byte(),
37:                         line: pos.row + 1,
38:                         column: pos.column + 1,
39:                         fix: Some(Fix::insert(child.start_byte(), ", ")),
40:                     });
41:                 }
42:                 prev_expr = None;
43:                 continue;
44:             }
45: 
46:             // Skip parentheses and other punctuation.
47:             if is_punctuation(kind) {
48:                 continue;
49:             }
50: 
51:             if let Some(prev) = prev_expr {
52:                 let gap = &source[prev.end_byte()..child.start_byte()];
53:                 if !gap.is_empty() && gap.chars().all(|c| c == ' ' || c == '\t') {
54:                     let pos = child.start_position();
55:                     let insert_pos = prev.end_byte();
56:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
57:                         rule_id: "NCOMMA",
58:                         message: "Use comma to separate input arguments".to_string(),
59:                         severity: Severity::Info,
60:                         byte_range: prev.end_byte()..child.start_byte(),
61:                         line: pos.row + 1,
62:                         column: pos.column + 1,
63:                         fix: Some(Fix::new(insert_pos..insert_pos + 1, ", ")),
64:                     });
65:                 }
66:             }
67:             prev_expr = Some(child);
68:         }
69:     }
70: }

11:     /// `switch_statement`, check that the `block` body is indented by
12:     /// `indent_size` spaces relative to the parent keyword.

14:         let parent_col = node.start_position().column;
15:         let expected_indent = parent_col + self.no4lp_config.indent_size;
16: 
17:         // Find all `block` children (there may be multiple in if/switch).
18:         let child_count = node.child_count();
19:         for i in 0..child_count {
20:             let Some(child) = node.child(i) else {
21:                 continue;
22:             };
23:             match child.kind() {
24:                 "block" => {
25:                     self.check_block_indentation(child, expected_indent, source, diagnostics);
26:                 }
27:                 // elseif_clause and else_clause also contain blocks.
28:                 "elseif_clause" | "else_clause" | "case_clause" | "otherwise_clause" => {
29:                     let inner_count = child.child_count();
30:                     for j in 0..inner_count {
31:                         if let Some(inner) = child.child(j) {
32:                             if inner.kind() == "block" {
33:                                 self.check_block_indentation(
34:                                     inner,
35:                                     expected_indent,
36:                                     source,
37:                                     diagnostics,
38:                                 );
39:                             }
40:                         }
41:                     }
42:                 }
43:                 _ => {}
44:             }
45:         }
46:     }

50:         &self,
51:         block: Node,

55:     ) {

1: //! NOCOMMA check: use commas to separate elements in a row.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl FormattingEngine {
6:     /// In `matrix` or `cell` nodes, check if `row` children have elements
7:     /// separated by spaces instead of commas. Look for adjacent expression
8:     /// nodes without a `,` between them.
9:     pub(crate) fn check_nocomma(
10:         &self,
11:         node: Node,
12:         source: &str,
13:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
14:     ) {
15:         let child_count = node.child_count();
16:         for i in 0..child_count {
17:             let Some(child) = node.child(i) else {
18:                 continue;
19:             };
20:             if child.kind() == "row" {
21:                 self.check_row_commas(child, source, diagnostics);
22:             }
23:         }
24:     }
25: 
26:     /// Check a single `row` node for missing commas between elements.
27:     fn check_row_commas(&self, row: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
28:         // Collect expression children (skip punctuation like "[", "]", ",", ";").
29:         let mut prev_expr: Option<Node> = None;
30:         let child_count = row.child_count();
31: 
32:         for i in 0..child_count {
33:             let Some(child) = row.child(i) else {
34:                 continue;
35:             };
36:             let kind = child.kind();
37: 
38:             // Reset tracking on comma or semicolon. A zero-width comma token
39:             // is inserted by the grammar when an element separator is missing.
40:             if kind == "," {
41:                 if child.start_byte() == child.end_byte() {
42:                     let pos = child.start_position();
43:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
44:                         rule_id: "NOCOMMA",
45:                         message: "Use commas to separate elements in a row".to_string(),
46:                         severity: Severity::Info,
47:                         byte_range: child.start_byte()..child.start_byte(),
48:                         line: pos.row + 1,
49:                         column: pos.column + 1,
50:                         fix: Some(Fix::insert(child.start_byte(), ", ")),
51:                     });
52:                 }
53:                 prev_expr = None;
54:                 continue;
55:             }
56:             if kind == ";" {
57:                 prev_expr = None;
58:                 continue;
59:             }
60: 
61:             // Skip non-expression tokens (brackets, whitespace nodes).
62:             if is_punctuation(kind) {
63:                 continue;
64:             }
65: 
66:             // If we have a previous expression and no comma was found between,
67:             // check whether there was only whitespace separating them.
68:             if let Some(prev) = prev_expr {
69:                 let gap = &source[prev.end_byte()..child.start_byte()];
70:                 if !gap.is_empty() && gap.chars().all(|c| c == ' ' || c == '\t') {
71:                     let pos = child.start_position();
72:                     let insert_pos = prev.end_byte();
73:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
74:                         rule_id: "NOCOMMA",
75:                         message: "Use commas to separate elements in a row".to_string(),
76:                         severity: Severity::Info,
77:                         byte_range: prev.end_byte()..child.start_byte(),
78:                         line: pos.row + 1,
79:                         column: pos.column + 1,
80:                         fix: Some(Fix::new(insert_pos..insert_pos + 1, ", ")),
81:                     });
82:                 }
83:             }
84:             prev_expr = Some(child);
85:         }
86:     }
87: }

1: //! NOPRT check: remove unnecessary parentheses.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
6: // NOPRT: Remove unnecessary parentheses
7: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
8: 
9: impl FormattingEngine {
10:     /// Detect `parenthesis` nodes that are unnecessary — e.g., `(x)` where
11:     /// x is a simple identifier or number, and the parenthesis is not a
12:     /// function call argument or condition.
13:     pub(crate) fn check_noprt(&self, node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
14:         // Only flag parenthesized simple expressions (identifier, number, string).
15:         let inner = find_inner_expr(node);
16:         let Some(inner_node) = inner else {
17:             return;
18:         };
19: 
20:         let inner_kind = inner_node.kind();
21:         if inner_kind != "identifier" && inner_kind != "number" && inner_kind != "string" {
22:             return;
23:         }
24: 
25:         // Don't flag if the parent is a function_call (arguments), or if it is
26:         // the condition of an if/while (that's NOPTS territory).
27:         if let Some(parent) = node.parent() {
28:             let pk = parent.kind();
29:             if pk == "function_call" || pk == "arguments" {
30:                 return;
31:             }
32:             // Skip if this is a condition node (handled by NOPTS).
33:             if (pk == "if_statement" || pk == "while_statement")
34:                 && parent
35:                     .child_by_field_name("condition")
36:                     .map(|c| c.id() == node.id())
37:                     .unwrap_or(false)
38:             {
39:                 return;
40:             }
41:         }
42: 
43:         let pos = node.start_position();
44:         let inner_text = &source[inner_node.start_byte()..inner_node.end_byte()];
45:         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
46:             rule_id: "NOPRT",
47:             message: format!("Unnecessary parentheses around '{}'", inner_text),
48:             severity: Severity::Info,
49:             byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
50:             line: pos.row + 1,
51:             column: pos.column + 1,
52:             fix: Some(Fix::new(
53:                 node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
54:                 inner_text.to_string(),
55:             )),
56:         });
57:     }

1: //! PRTCAL check: consider using command syntax instead of function syntax.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
6: // PRTCAL: Consider using command syntax
7: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
8: 
9: impl FormattingEngine {
10:     /// For `function_call` nodes at statement level with only string literal
11:     /// arguments, suggest command syntax instead. For example:
12:     /// `disp('hello')` could be `disp hello`.
13:     pub(crate) fn check_prtcal(&self, node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
14:         // Only fire at statement level.
15:         let is_statement_level = node
16:             .parent()
17:             .map(|p| STATEMENT_PARENTS.contains(&p.kind()))
18:             .unwrap_or(false);
19:         if !is_statement_level {
20:             return;
21:         }
22: 
23:         // Must have an arguments node with only string/identifier children.
24:         let Some(args_node) = find_arguments_child(node) else {
25:             return;
26:         };
27: 
28:         let mut arg_texts = Vec::new();
29:         let mut all_strings = true;
30:         let arg_count = args_node.child_count();
31:         let mut expr_count = 0;
32: 
33:         for i in 0..arg_count {
34:             let Some(arg) = args_node.child(i) else {
35:                 continue;
36:             };
37:             let kind = arg.kind();
38:             // Skip punctuation (parens, commas).
39:             if is_punctuation(kind) || kind == "," {
40:                 continue;
41:             }
42:             expr_count += 1;
43:             if kind == "string" {
44:                 // Extract string content without quotes.
45:                 let text = &source[arg.start_byte()..arg.end_byte()];
46:                 let unquoted = text
47:                     .trim_start_matches('\'')
48:                     .trim_end_matches('\'')
49:                     .trim_start_matches('"')
50:                     .trim_end_matches('"');
51:                 // Command syntax only works for simple strings without spaces.
52:                 if unquoted.contains(' ') || unquoted.contains('\'') {
53:                     all_strings = false;
54:                     break;
55:                 }
56:                 arg_texts.push(unquoted.to_string());
57:             } else {
58:                 all_strings = false;
59:                 break;
60:             }
61:         }
62: 
63:         // Must have at least one argument, and all must be simple strings.
64:         if expr_count == 0 || !all_strings {

1: //! # CONFIG_ISSUES_ENGINE: Configuration Issue Checks
2: //!
3: //! ```mlt
4: //! id = "CONFIG_ISSUES_ENGINE"
5: //! title = "Configuration Issues"
6: //! category = "configuration-issues"
7: //! severity = "error"
8: //! fix = false
9: //! icon = "lucide/cog"
10: //! slug = "config-issues"
11: //! ```
12: //!
13: //! ## Rule
14: //!
15: //! Detects MATLAB-side configuration issues such as invalid parameter names
16: //! passed to configuration functions, wrong argument counts, and invalid
17: //! option values. The engine matches `function_call` and `command` nodes
18: //! against known configuration function patterns and emits a diagnostic with
19: //! the specific check ID (`BDCFG`, `CFERR`, `BDOPT`, `CFIG`).
20: //!
21: //! ## Check IDs
22: //!
23: //! | Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description |
24: //! | --- | --- | --- | --- |
25: //! | BDCFG | error | no | Code Analyzer configuration file is invalid. Factory configuration is used instead. Run matlab.codeanalysis.validateConfiguration(VAR_NAME) to identify specific issues. |
26: //! | CFERR | error | no | Cannot open or read the Code Analyzer settings from file VAR_FILE. Using default settings instead. |
27: //! | BDOPT | error | no | Option VAR_NAME is ignored because it is invalid. |
28: //! | CFIG | error | no | The Code Analyzer settings file, VAR_FILE, has an error on line VAR_NUMBER. |
29: //!
30: //! ## Examples
31: //!
32: //! ### Incorrect
33: //!
34: //! ```matlab
35: //! set_param(gcs, 'NotARealParam', 'value');
36: //! cfg = coder.config('something');
37: //! opts = optimset('NotAnOption', 1);
38: //! ```
39: //!
40: //! ### Correct
41: //!
42: //! ```matlab
43: //! set_param(gcs, 'SimulationCommand', 'start');
44: //! cfg = coder.config('lib');
45: //! opts = optimset('Display', 'off');
46: //! ```
47: //!
48: //! ## Configuration
49: //!
50: //! ```toml
51: //! [lint.rules.CONFIG_ISSUES_ENGINE]
52: //! disabled_checks = []
53: //! ```

1: //! # UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE: Unset Variables
2: //!
3: //! ```mlt
4: //! id = "UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE"
5: //! title = "Unset Variables"
6: //! category = "unset-variables"
7: //! severity = "warning"
8: //! fix = false
9: //! icon = "lucide/alert-triangle"
10: //! slug = "unset-variables"
11: //! ```
12: //!
13: //! ## Rule
14: //!
15: //! Detects variables that might not be defined before use. A single file-level
16: //! engine (`UnsetVariablesEngine`) builds a symbol table and runs
17: //! definite-assignment analysis to find variables used on code paths where
18: //! they may never have been assigned. It covers 6 checks from MATLAB's "Unset
19: //! Variables" category; each diagnostic carries the specific check ID (e.g.
20: //! `NODEF`, `PSET`, `STOUT`).
21: //!
22: //! ## Check IDs
23: //!
24: //! | Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description |
25: //! | --- | --- | --- | --- |
26: //! | NODEF | warning | no | Variable might be used before it is defined. |
27: //! | USENS | warning | no | Explicitly initialize this variable to avoid a potential uninitialized variable, or use a valid syntax for function call on line VAR_NUMBER. |
28: //! | PSET | warning | no | Persistent variable is used, but might be unset. |
29: //! | SUSENS | warning | no | Variable is used, but might be unset (within a script). |
30: //! | SVNODEF | warning | no | Variable might not have a value, because variable definition may not be executed. |
31: //! | STOUT | warning | no | Function return value might be unset. |
32: //!
33: //! ## Examples
34: //!
35: //! ### Incorrect
36: //!
37: //! ```matlab
38: //! function f()
39: //!     disp(x);    % NODEF: x may never be defined before use
40: //! end
41: //!
42: //! function y = g()
43: //!     if flag
44: //!         y = 1;
45: //!     end         % STOUT: output not assigned on all paths
46: //! end
47: //! ```
48: //!
49: //! ### Correct
50: //!
51: //! ```matlab
52: //! function f()
53: //!     x = 0;
54: //!     disp(x);
55: //! end
56: //!
57: //! function y = g()
58: //!     y = 0;
59: //!     if flag
60: //!         y = 1;
61: //!     end
62: //! end
63: //! ```
64: //!
65: //! ## Configuration
66: //!
67: //! ```toml
68: //! [lint.rules.UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE]
69: //! severity = "warning"
70: //! ignore = ["myGlobalWorkspaceVar"]
71: //! ```

135: /// File-level rule engine that detects variables that might not be defined
136: /// before use. Emits diagnostics under multiple check IDs depending on context.
137: pub struct UnsetVariablesEngine {
138:     /// Rule-specific configuration (retained for future use / serialization).
139:     _config: UnsetVariablesConfig,

141:     ignore_set: HashSet<String>,

144: impl UnsetVariablesEngine {
145:     /// Factory constructor — reads rule-specific params from config.
146:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
147:         let rule_config: UnsetVariablesConfig = config.rule_params("UNSET_VARIABLES_ENGINE");
148:         let mut ignore_set: HashSet<String> =
149:             MATLAB_BUILTINS.iter().map(|s| (*s).to_string()).collect();
150:         for name in &rule_config.ignore {
151:             ignore_set.insert(name.clone());
152:         }
153:         Box::new(Self {
154:             _config: rule_config,
155:             ignore_set,
156:         })
157:     }

159:     /// Check whether a variable name should be ignored.
160:     pub(crate) fn is_ignored(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
161:         self.ignore_set.contains(name)

163: 
164:     /// Find the location of the first assignment to a variable within a compound
165:     /// statement (for PSET diagnostic positioning).
166:     pub(crate) fn find_assignment_location(
167:         &self,
168:         node: Node,
169:         source: &str,
170:         var_name: &str,
171:     ) -> Option<(std::ops::Range<usize>, usize, usize)> {
172:         // DFS search for the first assignment to var_name.
173:         let mut stack = vec![node];
174:         while let Some(current) = stack.pop() {
175:             if current.kind() == "assignment" {
176:                 if let Some(lhs) = current.child_by_field_name("left") {
177:                     if lhs.kind() == "identifier" {
178:                         let name = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
179:                         if name == var_name {
180:                             let pos = lhs.start_position();
181:                             return Some((
182:                                 lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte(),
183:                                 pos.row + 1,
184:                                 pos.column + 1,
185:                             ));
186:                         }
187:                     }
188:                 }
189:             }

4:     /// Check an if_statement for partial assignment (PSET).
5:     pub(crate) fn check_if_pset(
6:         &self,
7:         node: Node,
8:         source: &str,
9:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
10:     ) {
11:         let mut branch_assignments: Vec<HashSet<String>> = Vec::new();
12:         let mut has_else = false;
13: 
14:         let count = node.child_count();
15:         for i in 0..count {
16:             let Some(child) = node.child(i) else {
17:                 continue;
18:             };
19:             match child.kind() {
20:                 "block" => {
21:                     // The main if-body block.
22:                     branch_assignments.push(collect_block_assignments(child, source));
23:                 }
24:                 "elseif_clause" => {
25:                     let inner_count = child.child_count();
26:                     for j in 0..inner_count {
27:                         if let Some(inner) = child.child(j) {
28:                             if inner.kind() == "block" {
29:                                 branch_assignments.push(collect_block_assignments(inner, source));
30:                                 break;
31:                             }
32:                         }
33:                     }
34:                 }
35:                 "else_clause" => {
36:                     has_else = true;
37:                     let inner_count = child.child_count();
38:                     for j in 0..inner_count {
39:                         if let Some(inner) = child.child(j) {
40:                             if inner.kind() == "block" {
41:                                 branch_assignments.push(collect_block_assignments(inner, source));
42:                                 break;
43:                             }
44:                         }
45:                     }
46:                 }
47:                 _ => {}
48:             }
49:         }
50: 
51:         // Only emit PSET if there's an else branch (complete coverage).
52:         if !has_else || branch_assignments.len() < 2 {
53:             return;
54:         }
55: 
56:         // Find variables assigned in some branches but not all.
57:         let all_vars: HashSet<String> = branch_assignments
58:             .iter()
59:             .flat_map(|s| s.iter().cloned())
60:             .collect();
61: 
62:         for var_name in &all_vars {
63:             if self.is_ignored(var_name) {
64:                 continue;
65:             }
66:             let assigned_in_all = branch_assignments.iter().all(|s| s.contains(var_name));
67:             if !assigned_in_all {
68:                 // Find the first branch that assigns this variable for location info.
69:                 if let Some(loc) = self.find_assignment_location(node, source, var_name) {
70:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
71:                         rule_id: "PSET",
72:                         message: format!(
73:                             "Variable '{}' is set in some branches but not all",
74:                             var_name
75:                         ),
76:                         severity: Severity::Warning,
77:                         byte_range: loc.0,
78:                         line: loc.1,
79:                         column: loc.2,
80:                         fix: None,
81:                     });
82:                 }

9: 
10:         for scope in &symbol_table.scopes {
11:             if scope.kind != ScopeKind::Script {
12:                 continue;
13:             }
14: 
15:             // In scripts, variables must be defined before use within the file.
16:             // We check for uses that appear before any definition.

18: 
19:             for var_use in &scope.uses {

21:                     continue;
22:                 }

24:                     continue;
25:                 }

27:                 // Find the earliest definition of this variable in the scope.
28:                 let earliest_def = scope
29:                     .defs
30:                     .iter()
31:                     .filter(|d| d.name == var_use.name)
32:                     .min_by_key(|d| d.byte_range.start);
33: 
34:                 match earliest_def {

48:                             fix: None,
49:                         });

4:     /// Check a switch_statement for partial assignment (PSET).
5:     pub(crate) fn check_switch_pset(
6:         &self,
7:         node: Node,
8:         source: &str,
9:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
10:     ) {
11:         let mut branch_assignments: Vec<HashSet<String>> = Vec::new();
12:         let mut has_otherwise = false;
13: 
14:         let count = node.child_count();
15:         for i in 0..count {
16:             let Some(child) = node.child(i) else {
17:                 continue;
18:             };
19:             match child.kind() {
20:                 "case_clause" => {
21:                     let inner_count = child.child_count();
22:                     for j in 0..inner_count {
23:                         if let Some(inner) = child.child(j) {
24:                             if inner.kind() == "block" {
25:                                 branch_assignments.push(collect_block_assignments(inner, source));
26:                                 break;
27:                             }
28:                         }
29:                     }
30:                 }
31:                 "otherwise_clause" => {
32:                     has_otherwise = true;
33:                     let inner_count = child.child_count();
34:                     for j in 0..inner_count {
35:                         if let Some(inner) = child.child(j) {
36:                             if inner.kind() == "block" {
37:                                 branch_assignments.push(collect_block_assignments(inner, source));
38:                                 break;
39:                             }
40:                         }
41:                     }
42:                 }
43:                 _ => {}
44:             }
45:         }
46: 
47:         // Only emit PSET if there's an otherwise clause.
48:         if !has_otherwise || branch_assignments.len() < 2 {
49:             return;
50:         }
51: 
52:         let all_vars: HashSet<String> = branch_assignments
53:             .iter()
54:             .flat_map(|s| s.iter().cloned())
55:             .collect();
56: 
57:         for var_name in &all_vars {
58:             if self.is_ignored(var_name) {
59:                 continue;
60:             }
61:             let assigned_in_all = branch_assignments.iter().all(|s| s.contains(var_name));
62:             if !assigned_in_all {
63:                 if let Some(loc) = self.find_assignment_location(node, source, var_name) {
64:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
65:                         rule_id: "PSET",
66:                         message: format!(
67:                             "Variable '{}' is set in some branches but not all",
68:                             var_name
69:                         ),
70:                         severity: Severity::Warning,
71:                         byte_range: loc.0,
72:                         line: loc.1,
73:                         column: loc.2,
74:                         fix: None,
75:                     });
76:                 }
77:             }
78:         }

1: //! # UNUSED_ENGINE: Unused Constructions
2: //!
3: //! ```mlt
4: //! id = "UNUSED_ENGINE"
5: //! title = "Unused Constructions"
6: //! category = "unused-constructions"
7: //! severity = "warning"
8: //! fix = false
9: //! icon = "lucide/trash-2"
10: //! slug = "unused"
11: //! ```
12: //!
13: //! ## Rule
14: //!
15: //! Detects unused variables, functions, methods, and dead code in MATLAB
16: //! files. A single file-level engine (`UnusedEngine`) builds a symbol table
17: //! and runs unreachability analysis, then cross-references every definition
18: //! against its usages to identify dead code. It covers 17 checks from
19: //! MATLAB's "Unused Constructions" category; each diagnostic carries the
20: //! specific check ID (e.g. `NASGU`, `UNRCH`, `MSNU`).
21: //!
22: //! ## Check IDs
23: //!
24: //! | Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description |
25: //! | --- | --- | --- | --- |
26: //! | NASGU | warning | no | Value assigned to variable might be unused. |
27: //! | NUSED | warning | no | Global or persistent variable might be unused or unset in this function or script. |
28: //! | NOEFF | warning | no | The operation or expression VAR_OPERATOR has no evident effect. |
29: //! | EQEFF | warning | no | To assign values to variables, use =. The == operator compares equality of values. |
30: //! | ASGLU | warning | no | Value assigned to variable might be unused. Consider replacing the variable with ~ instead. |
31: //! | SETNU | warning | no | Variable is set, but might be unused. |
32: //! | PUSE | warning | no | Persistent variable might be unused. |
33: //! | PREALL | warning | no | The preallocated value assigned to variable might be unused. |
34: //! | INUSA | warning | no | Input argument might be unused after the function arguments block(s). |
35: //! | INUSD | warning | no | Input argument might be unused. Consider replacing the argument with ~ instead. |
36: //! | VANUS | info | no | Input argument 'varargin' might be unused. |
37: //! | DEFNU | warning | no | Function might be unused. |
38: //! | UNRCH | warning | no | This statement (and possibly following ones) cannot be reached. |
39: //! | MANU | warning | no | Input argument might be unused. Consider replacing the argument with ~, or make this method Static instead. |
40: //! | VUNUS | warning | no | VAR_OPERATOR produces a value that might be unused. |
41: //! | MSNU | warning | no | A Code Analyzer message was once suppressed here, but the message is no longer generated. |
42: //! | MSNE | info | no | No Code Analyzer check is found for this check ID. |
43: //!
44: //! ## Examples
45: //!
46: //! ### Incorrect
47: //!
48: //! ```matlab
49: //! function f()
50: //!     temp = compute();   % NASGU: assigned but never used
51: //!     x = 1;
52: //!     return;
53: //!     y = x;              % UNRCH: unreachable after return
54: //!     s.field = 1;        % MSNU: set but never read
55: //! end
56: //! ```
57: //!
58: //! ### Correct
59: //!
60: //! ```matlab
61: //! function f()
62: //!     x = compute();
63: //!     disp(x);
64: //!     s.field = x;
65: //!     disp(s.field);
66: //! end
67: //! ```
68: //!
69: //! ## Configuration
70: //!
71: //! ```toml
72: //! [lint.rules.UNUSED_ENGINE]
73: //! severity = "warning"
74: //! ignore_patterns = ["_*", "unused*"]
75: //! disabled_checks = ["VANUS"]
76: //! ```

156: /// File-level rule engine for detecting unused constructions.

159: /// and running unreachability analysis, then cross-referencing definitions with
160: /// usages to identify dead code.

167:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
168:         let rule_config: UnusedConfig = config.rule_params("UNUSED_ENGINE");
169:         Box::new(Self {

175:     fn is_check_disabled(&self, check_id: &str) -> bool {
176:         self.config
177:             .disabled_checks
178:             .iter()
179:             .any(|d| d.eq_ignore_ascii_case(check_id))
180:     }

182:     /// Check if a variable name should be ignored based on configured patterns.
183:     fn should_ignore_name(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
184:         // Always ignore `_` and names starting with `~`.
185:         if name == "_" || name.starts_with('~') {
186:             return true;
187:         }
188:         // Always ignore MATLAB built-in specials.
189:         if ALWAYS_USED.contains(&name) {
190:             return true;
191:         }
192:         // Check configured patterns.
193:         self.config
194:             .ignore_patterns
195:             .iter()
196:             .any(|pat| matches_simple_glob(pat, name))
197:     }

199:     /// Run MSNU check: struct field set but never read.
200:     /// This is a heuristic check based on field_expression analysis.
201:     fn check_msnu(&self, ctx: &FileContext, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
202:         if self.is_check_disabled("MSNU") {
203:             return;
204:         }
205: 
206:         let mut field_writes: Vec<FieldAccess> = Vec::new();
207:         let mut field_reads: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
208: 
209:         Self::collect_field_accesses(
210:             ctx.tree.root_node(),
211:             ctx.source,
212:             &mut field_writes,
213:             &mut field_reads,
214:         );
215: 
216:         // Report fields that are written but never read.
217:         for write in &field_writes {
218:             let key = format!("{}.{}", write.object, write.field);
219:             if !field_reads.contains(&key) {
220:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
221:                     rule_id: "MSNU",
222:                     message: format!(
223:                         "Struct field '{}.{}' is set but never read",
224:                         write.object, write.field
225:                     ),
226:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
227:                     byte_range: write.byte_range.clone(),
228:                     line: write.line,
229:                     column: write.column,
230:                     fix: None,
231:                 });
232:             }
233:         }
234:     }

236:     /// Run MSNE check: struct field doesn't exist (assigned but potential typo).
237:     /// Heuristic: if a struct has many fields and one is only written once with
238:     /// no reads, it may be a typo.
239:     fn check_msne(&self, ctx: &FileContext, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
240:         if self.is_check_disabled("MSNE") {
241:             return;
242:         }
243: 
244:         let mut field_writes: Vec<FieldAccess> = Vec::new();
245:         let mut field_reads: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
246: 
247:         Self::collect_field_accesses(
248:             ctx.tree.root_node(),
249:             ctx.source,
250:             &mut field_writes,
251:             &mut field_reads,
252:         );
253: 
254:         // Group writes by object name.
255:         let mut writes_by_object: HashMap<&str, Vec<&FieldAccess>> = HashMap::new();
256:         for write in &field_writes {
257:             writes_by_object
258:                 .entry(write.object.as_str())
259:                 .or_default()
260:                 .push(write);
261:         }
262: 
263:         // For each object with multiple fields written, check if any field
264:         // is written exactly once and never read — potential typo.
265:         for (object, writes) in &writes_by_object {
266:             if writes.len() < 2 {
267:                 continue;
268:             }
269: 
270:             let mut field_write_count: HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new();
271:             for w in writes {
272:                 *field_write_count.entry(w.field.as_str()).or_insert(0) += 1;
273:             }
274: 
275:             for w in writes {
276:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", object, w.field);
277:                 if field_write_count.get(w.field.as_str()) == Some(&1)
278:                     && !field_reads.contains(&key)
279:                 {
280:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
281:                         rule_id: "MSNE",
282:                         message: format!(
283:                             "Struct field '{}.{}' is assigned once and never read (possible typo)",
284:                             object, w.field
285:                         ),
286:                         severity: Severity::Info,
287:                         byte_range: w.byte_range.clone(),
288:                         line: w.line,
289:                         column: w.column,
290:                         fix: None,
291:                     });
292:                 }
293:             }
294:         }
295:     }

297:     /// Collect field accesses (both reads and writes) from the parse tree.
298:     fn collect_field_accesses(
299:         node: Node,
300:         source: &str,
301:         writes: &mut Vec<FieldAccess>,
302:         reads: &mut HashSet<String>,
303:     ) {
304:         if node.kind() == "assignment" {
305:             // Check if LHS is a field_expression.
306:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
307:                 if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
308:                     if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(lhs, source) {
309:                         writes.push(access);
310:                     }
311:                 }
312:             }
313:             // Check RHS for field reads.
314:             if let Some(rhs) = node.child_by_field_name("right") {
315:                 Self::collect_field_reads(rhs, source, reads);
316:             }
317:         } else if node.kind() == "field_expression" {
318:             // A field_expression not on the LHS of assignment is a read.
319:             if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(node, source) {
320:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", access.object, access.field);
321:                 reads.insert(key);
322:             }
323:         }
324: 
325:         // Recurse into children (skip assignment children we already handled).
326:         if node.kind() != "assignment" {
327:             let count = node.child_count();
328:             for i in 0..count {
329:                 if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
330:                     Self::collect_field_accesses(child, source, writes, reads);
331:                 }
332:             }
333:         } else {
334:             // For assignments, recurse into children except LHS field_expression.
335:             let count = node.child_count();
336:             for i in 0..count {
337:                 if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
338:                     if child.kind() == "field_expression" {
339:                         if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
340:                             if lhs.id() == child.id() {
341:                                 continue;
342:                             }
343:                         }
344:                     }
345:                     Self::collect_field_accesses(child, source, writes, reads);
346:                 }
347:             }
348:         }
349:     }

351:     /// Collect field reads from an expression subtree.
352:     fn collect_field_reads(node: Node, source: &str, reads: &mut HashSet<String>) {
353:         if node.kind() == "field_expression" {
354:             if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(node, source) {
355:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", access.object, access.field);
356:                 reads.insert(key);
357:             }
358:         }
359: 
360:         let count = node.child_count();
361:         for i in 0..count {
362:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
363:                 Self::collect_field_reads(child, source, reads);
364:             }
365:         }
366:     }

467: pub(crate) fn matches_simple_glob(pattern: &str, text: &str) -> bool {

475:     if pi == pat.len() {
476:         return ti == txt.len();

479:     match pat[pi] {
480:         '*' => {
481:             // `*` matches zero or more characters.

491:             if ti < txt.len() {

493:             } else {
494:                 false
495:             }
496:         }
497:         c => {

499:                 glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, ti + 1)
500:             } else {
501:                 false
502:             }
503:         }
504:     }

29: /// Recursively walk tree to find statement-level expressions with no effect.

31:     node: Node,
32:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
33:     noeff_disabled: bool,
34:     eqeff_disabled: bool,
35: ) {
36:     // Check if this node is at statement level (parent is block or source_file).
37:     let is_statement_level = node
38:         .parent()
39:         .map(|p| STATEMENT_PARENTS.contains(&p.kind()))
40:         .unwrap_or(false);
41: 
42:     if is_statement_level {
43:         let kind = node.kind();
44: 
45:         // EQEFF: comparison operator at statement level.
46:         if !eqeff_disabled && kind == COMPARISON_NODE {
47:             let pos = node.start_position();

49:                 rule_id: "EQEFF",

51:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
52:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
53:                 line: pos.row + 1,
54:                 column: pos.column + 1,
55:                 fix: None,
56:             });
57:         }
58:         // NOEFF: other expression nodes at statement level that are not
59:         // assignments, function_calls, or commands.
60:         else if !noeff_disabled && NO_EFFECT_EXPR_NODES.contains(&kind) {
61:             let pos = node.start_position();
